name: Siddhartha Gautama
role: Prince of the Shakya clan, raised at Kapilavastu, who left the palace at twenty-nine and became the Buddha after years of seeking.
fun_fact: His clan name, Gautama, and his people, the Shakyas, are why he is often called Shakyamuni, the sage of the Shakyas.

name: The Buddha
role: The awakened teacher whose life and teaching gave rise to the Buddhist tradition, honoured across Asia as Shakyamuni and as one buddha among many.
fun_fact: The title Buddha means awakened one, so it describes what he became rather than serving as a personal name.

name: Maya
role: Queen of the Shakya king Suddhodana and mother of the Buddha, remembered for her dream of the white elephant and her death a week after the birth.
fun_fact: She is said to have given birth while standing and holding a sal tree branch, a pose that became common in Asian sculpture.

name: Mara
role: The tempter who tries to stop the Buddha's awakening, described both as a lord of the desire realm and as the personified force of craving, fear and death.
fun_fact: His name is linked to the word for death, and the Pali verses list his armies as inner states such as doubt, sloth and the hunger for praise.

name: Ananda
role: The Buddha's cousin and longtime attendant, remembered for his memory and for reciting the discourses at the first council after the Buddha's death.
fun_fact: The suttas open with the words 'Thus have I heard', the formula through which Ananda's recitation of the teaching is remembered.

name: Angulimala
role: A murderer who became a monk after the Buddha confronted him on a forest road, and whose story tests what forgiveness can and cannot repair.
fun_fact: His birth name was Ahimsaka, meaning harmless, a name the story deliberately sets against the man he later became.

name: Kisa Gotami
role: A grieving mother in the Dhammapada commentary who carries her dead son through the city and learns from the mustard seed that loss is shared.
fun_fact: Her name means lean Gotami, and the mustard seed she was sent to find has become a byword for a grief that everyone carries.

name: Nigrodha, the Banyan Deer
role: The Bodhisatta in the Nigrodhamiga Jataka, a deer king who offers his own life so that a pregnant doe may live to give birth.
fun_fact: He is one of the Jataka births in which the Bodhisatta appears as an animal rather than as a human being.

name: Yasodhara
role: Siddhartha's wife and the mother of Rahula, who is left sleeping in the palace on the night he departs and later becomes a nun.
fun_fact: Sanskrit sources also call her Gopa or Bimba, and later tradition tells of her own path to awakening after the Buddha left.

name: Rahula
role: The son of Siddhartha and Yasodhara, born on the night of the departure, who was later ordained and became one of the Buddha's closest disciples.
fun_fact: His name means fetter, and the texts say his father spoke the word when he heard that a son had been born.
